beats.text: A chemist measured the age of the Earth.
beats.note: Clair Patterson used lead from the Canyon Diablo meteorite and got 4.55 billion years, give or take 70 million.

beats.text: His samples kept coming out contaminated.
beats.note: He found lead throughout his laboratory, even in his own hair.

beats.text: He built one of the first clean rooms.
beats.note: He acid-cleaned his apparatus and distilled every chemical shipped to him.

beats.text: The lead in the air was not natural.
beats.note: Ice cores from Greenland in 1964 and Antarctica in 1965 showed atmospheric lead rising soon after tetraethyl lead was introduced.

beats.text: Modern bones held far more lead than ancient ones.
beats.note: He reported a rise of 700 to 1200 fold against 1600 year old Peruvian skeletons.
He was excluded from a 1971 National Research Council panel on atmospheric lead.

beats.name: Leaded petrol
beats.role: Completely banned for road vehicles in the United States on 1 January 1996.

beats.text: He set out to date the Earth and ended up cleaning its air.

beats.line: Fix the noise before you read the signal.
